assessment: The response is a well-structured, actionable recommendation (free shipping at $85) with a profit-focused metric, clear decision rules, and solid UX advice. However, a majority of judges independently confirmed a material calculation error: the 15% discount scenario applies the 42% margin to discounted revenue instead of holding COGS constant, overstating contribution ($25.70 vs. correct $19.44) and understating breakeven volume lift (17.7% vs. ~56%). The recommendation itself survives and is arguably strengthened by the corrected math. Remaining weaknesses include non-exhaustive decision bands, underpowered test design for small stores, assumption-based breakeven projections, and unaddressed risks such as returns, shipping-cost variability, and customer expectation anchoring.
judge_agreement: All five judges agreed the plan is concrete and actionable with a sound directional recommendation, and none identified rule errors. Judges disagreed sharply on severity: anthropic and openai both detected the same discount-margin calculation error and scored specificity 4-6, while google, deepseek, and qwen (which explicitly verified the flawed math as correct) scored 9-10. Google was a consistent high outlier across all criteria (10/10/10), while openai was a consistent low outlier (6/4/5).
